title: HOW TO PRAY IN A CRISIS

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Jacob prayed, 'O God of my father Abraham, God of my father Isaac, LORD, you who said to me, "Go back to your country and your relatives, and I will make you prosper," I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown your servant. I had only my staff when I crossed this Jordan, but now I have become two camps. Save me, I pray, from the hand of my brother Esau, for I am afraid he will come and attack me, and also the mothers with their children. But you have said, "I will surely make you prosper and will make your descendants like the sand of the sea, which cannot be counted."'" - Gen 32:9-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Facing the greatest crisis of his life, Jacob prays — and his prayer is a beautiful model for us. Look at how he prays. First, he reminds God of who He is and what He has said: "you who said to me, 'Go back... and I will make you prosper.'" Jacob had obeyed God's command; now he holds God to God's own word.

Then Jacob humbles himself: "I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness you have shown." He does not come demanding, but grateful, remembering that he had crossed the Jordan years ago with nothing but a staff, and now had so much. He counts God's past mercies before asking for more.

Next comes his honest, specific request: "Save me, I pray, from the hand of my brother Esau." No vague words — he names his real fear and asks plainly for rescue. And he ends by anchoring himself again in God's promise: "you have said, 'I will surely make you prosper.'"

Here is a pattern worth following in our own crises: remember who God is, humbly recall His past kindness, ask honestly for what we need, and rest on His promises. When distress presses in, do not merely worry — pray like this. Bring God's own promises back to Him, and let them steady your trembling heart.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do my prayers rest on God's promises and past faithfulness?
2. Am I honest and specific with God about my real fears?
3. How can I pray like Jacob the next time crisis comes?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to pray as Jacob did — remembering who You are, recalling Your kindness, asking honestly, and resting on Your promises. Steady my heart as I bring my fears to You. Amen.
